questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The USA has a huge impact on the rest of the western world. Hence, I think it is important to have a fair impression of this nation, it's people and the American culture.
Then I also know that the USA is very strong in physics, so that is a good bonus.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy, both the people in Illinois and in Copenhagen that had to help me where very help full.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a huge welcoming event for all incoming exchange students and my administrative college also hosted a lot of social events.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Various dorms and some private housing as well.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Bad cooking facilities but pretty good meal plans where available.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You will get to know your neighbours. And the walls can be very thin some times.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You are enrolled as an undergraduate student, so if enrolling in graduate courses, you have to proove that you are a graduate student at your home institution. This is easy. If you are not a physics student. In which case you will have to convince two people simultaneously that you are a graduate student. And they are not exchaging information. Very frustrating.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The physics administration, but they were not super efficient. An easy fix was to simply show up at the grad-student administration office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not  very, but there where some good alternatives. The Physics department's administration at UIUC is super annoying though. It was very hard to convince them that I was a graduate student.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be in good time, and send all information to everybody you have to contact. Also in the US, you can try out different class and change course concurrently. So give everything that seems interesting a shot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The physics courses is on a comparable (maybe slightly lower) level compared to copenhagen. But they are still very challenging. The graduate statistics course I took was very easy though and I have heard similar stories from other students in order majors.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot more sitting in class rooms and following the flow of the lecturer. At UCPH you can study the way that suits you bet, but that is not an option at UIUC. You very much have to follow the structure of the classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Computational Statistics (STAT 525)
Condensed Matter Physics 1 (PHYS 560)
Introduction to Subatomic Physics (PHYS 470)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of the above are pretty good, especially the STAT 525.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had great fun running with the Track and Field Club.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Whatever you desire.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Whatever you desire.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See the Amish that live in Arthur Illinois. It is a very interesting experience.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It takes some getting used to. I think I had a good group of friends after 3-4 weeks. And my neighbours were very nice.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer:
Do it!
Americans a very approachable so go to them say hello. Talk and you will do well. Also find somebody to do something with. I found some gym-bros to go running and training with.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Americans are approachable but very hard to "really" get to know. Unlike danes who are unapproachable, but once you get them drunk they start talking.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
It was very nice and "low-stakes" to hang out with americans in the Track and Field club.
Partying with european exchange students was amazing :)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1: Talk to people, they are friendly and approachable on average (and you will go crazy if you don't.)
2: Remember to party, I spent too much time studying. And exams are easier in the US than in Denmark :)
3: Make sure to get around the US while you are there. It is an amazing, beuatiful and shockingly large country.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take chances. Remember you are only there for 4-8 months. And it is pretty low stakes. So try to get to know yourself and make some friends and connections from all over the world. This is not the time for hiding away in your room.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the connection I know have both in Europe, The US and East Asia as a result of having gone on exchange.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first few weeks where you do not yet have a network are pretty tough.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
